key_insight: Tail-CRC separates budget-constrained answer generation from abstention, using a single rollout to control expected wrong submissions under exchangeability.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can recalibrate submission risk across targets or domains without retraining the solver or paying for multiple inference samples.
method: Adapt the solver to budget forcing with binary correctness rewards, then freeze it.
Score uncertainty using upper-tail token surprise within the generated answer.
Apply conformal risk control to decide whether to submit or abstain.
evidence_signal: Across two Qwen models, 50 RL updates on 400 problems improved correct-submission rates by 15.0–29.6 percentage points on DAPO; target-domain calibration reduced 8B Omni-MATH wrong submissions from 30.3% to 5.8% at 4K tokens.
watch_item: The guarantee concerns expected wrong submissions under exchangeability, not error rates among submitted answers; domain shifts require careful recalibration.
paper_title: Decoupling Solving from Abstention: Single-Rollout Conformal Risk Control for Hard-Budget LLM Reasoning
